candidate: External SHA-bound safetensors sidecar for the Marlin W4 shortlist scan
scope: Qwen3.5-0.8B GPTQ-Marlin, RTX 4060 Laptop SM89, greedy active batch 1

architecture.offline: Convert the checkpoint FP16 tied embedding to the runtime BF16 value, quantize with vLLM production GPTQ APIs, repack for Marlin and store packed_weight plus permuted_scales.
architecture.runtime: Require an exact sidecar SHA-256, validate schema/shape/dtype/quantization metadata, load tensors directly to the target CUDA device, allocate only the Marlin workspace and warm the existing rerank op during weight post-processing.

production_smoke.protocol: fresh VLLM_CACHE_ROOT, one warmup and one measured 64-token greedy request; discovery evidence only

technical_failure_and_repair.cause: Placing the sidecar inside the Hugging Face model directory made vLLM discover it as a second checkpoint shard and reject its non-model tensor names.
technical_failure_and_repair.repair: Move sidecars to a dedicated external directory and make the builder reject output.parent == checkpoint.parent.

global_value.priority: Useful for production hardening and frequent cold starts, but lower global value than a new steady-state decode architecture.

why: The input embedding reads rows from the same tied BF16 parameter.
The top-128 rerank reads original BF16 rows to recover higher-fidelity scores.
Removing the dense table therefore requires a quantized embedding and eliminates the current BF16 rerank authority, creating a different numerical candidate.
memory_boundary.conclusion: Checkpoint-native loading and shared-weight compression are separate architecture decisions; only the former is proven here.

decision: Keep as an incremental production-hardening patch on top of the already qualified approximate rerank candidate. Do not claim a new throughput optimum or a memory reduction. Rebuild the sidecar for every checkpoint and require the recorded SHA-256 at runtime.
